Caliph Abu Bakr's Appointment of Caliph Umar and the Six-Man Shura
hook: Caliph Abu Bakr left Caliph Umar in his place. Caliph Umar in turn gave the matter to six people; this shura is narrated in Bukhari.
scenes.0.text: C**aliph** Abu Bakr fell seriously ill in Medina at the end of his caliphate, which lasted just over two years. When he realized that his death was imminent, he wanted to determine who would succeed him and appointed Umar as caliph. The administration was hastily installed in Sakife, so it changed hands from one person to another. In this assignment, His Holiness Ali's opinion was not asked and he was not called upon to make this decision. It was the second time in Ghadir Hum that the Prophet raised his hand in front of thousands of people. Ali was patient again for the unity of the Ummah.

scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7

scenes.1.text: Abu Bekir consulted with **Abdurrahman b. Avf** and Uthman before making this decision. Some of the Sahaba, who knew of Umar's harsh disposition, were worried about this election. **Talha** objected and asked Abu Bakr, "What would you say to your Lord if you brought such a harsh person upon us?" And Abu Bakr informed Allah that he would tell Allah that He had chosen the best of His servants. Among those consulted were the Prophet's uncle's son and son-in-law, **Ali**. The Ahl-i-Bait's opinion was never taken into account in this decision.

scenes.2.text: Abu Bakr passed away on the 22nd of the month of Jamezilahir, in the 13th year of the Hijrah. He had been c**aliph** for about two years and three months. Then Umar became caliph. During his reign, Islamic territory expanded rapidly, conquering Iraq, Syria, and Egypt. Ali lived in Medina during these years. The caliph consulted him from time to time on difficult matters. But consultation was no substitute for the leadership declared in Ghadir. Ali did not draw his sword for his right and waited quietly in his house so that there would be no division among the Ummah. As the conquests grew, the Prophet's guardian spent his days patiently at his home in Medina.

scenes.3.text: In the 23rd year of the Hijrah, C**aliph** Umar was stabbed during a morning prayer in Medina. The attacker wounded thirteen others at the mosque. **Ömer** moved to his home severely wounded and died a few days later, on the 26th of Zilhicce. His caliphate lasted about ten years and six months. He didn't choose his successor alone on his deathbed. Instead, he decided to leave the job to a six-person board. Ali would be among those six. But the rules of the council would eventually exclude him from the succession again.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7

scenes.4.text: The wounded Umar counted the six people who would attend: Hz. **Ali**, Uthman, Zubeir, **Talha**, Sa'd b. His son Abdullah will attend as a witness, but will not be elected as caliph. His Holiness Ali, who had been declared worthy of the honor, was made an ordinary member of this council. Being on the board didn't mean being elected.

scenes.5.text: Six people gathered in a room. The discussions lasted a few days. Zubair left his right to **Ali**. **Talha** left his right to Uthman. Sa'd b. Abi Vakkas also transferred his rights to **Abdurrahman b. Avf**. So, we are left with Ali, Uthman and Abdurrahman. The choice was now in Abdurrahman's hands. He took a promise from Ali and Uthman that they would obey whoever was chosen. Now the leader of the nation would be chosen by one person.

scenes.6.text: 'Abd al-Rahman first turned to '**Ali** and offered him a condition: that he would be faithful to the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of the Prophet and the way of the previous two caliphs. A pledge of allegiance. Ali replied, "By the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Prophet, and by my own tradition". He didn't take the path of the previous two caliphs as a condition. He didn't want to follow the trail of the unjust caliphs, he wanted to follow the trail of the Prophet. This answer closed the door of the caliphate to him once again. Abdurrahman offered the same condition to Uthman. Uthman, for the sake of position and position, preferred to follow the path of the unjust caliphs and accepted the condition without any hesitation. Abdurrahman then pledged his allegiance to Uthman and the others followed.

scenes.7.text: Thus Uthman became the third c**aliph**. Years later, in his sermon known as Shikshakyye, Ali would tell of these days with sorrow. He complained that Umar considered himself one of those six and treated him like one of them. He also said that the order of this room predetermined the outcome from the beginning. From Sakife to there, his rights were suspended three times. Yet he did not draw the sword, but he kept the unity of the nation before his own right. In this sermon, Ali says that he spent those years patiently with a thorn in his eye and a bone in his throat.

sunni.0.says: Caliph Umar is wounded; he designates Ali, Uthman, Zubayr, Talha, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman b. Awf; Zubayr and Talha withdraw in favor of Ali and Uthman, Sa'd in favor of Abd al-Rahman; Abd al-Rahman takes a promise from both to rule with justice and obey whoever is chosen, chooses Uthman, and Ali pledges allegiance.
sunni.1.says: Caliph Abu Bakr's consultation with Abd al-Rahman b. Awf and Uthman; the objection of a group of Companions about Caliph Umar's harshness (seen secondarily in an IslamQA summary).
sunni.2.says: Caliph Abu Bakr's testament, Caliph Umar's shura, Abd al-Rahman's condition of "the Book of God, the sunna, the conduct of the two shaykhs," and Ali's answer "my own ijtihad" (it has variants).
sunni.3.says: Talha's objection to Caliph Umar's appointment (seen secondarily as an attribution on WikiShia and various sites).
sunni.4.says: Details of the shura and Uthman's pledge.
shia.0.says: Ali's complaint about the caliphate's period, the caliph Umar's council and his being counted as one of them. Summary from WikiShia.
shia.1.says: The claim that the sermon appears with a chain of transmission in sources before al-Radi (from a WikiShia summary; the books themselves were not opened).
shia.2.says: A Mu'tazili commentator; he says he saw the sermon in the works of authors before al-Radi such as al-Balkhi and Ibn Qutayba (WikiShia report).
shia.3.says: The concept of the Shi'ite Imamate and all the references to it.
disputes.0.title: gr3wv8
Can a caliph appoint his own successor?
disputes.0.sunni: Caliph Abu Bakr chose Caliph Umar in his place; this appointment is narrated in the sources. In the Sunni reading, this is a legitimate path through the benefit of the Ummah and the acceptance of the Companions.
disputes.0.shia: Caliph Abu Bakr chose Caliph Umar in his place; this appointment is narrated in the sources. In the Shia reading, the place of the caliphate lies with Imam Ali through the testament at Ghadir.
disputes.1.title: 50n32k
The six of the shura
disputes.1.sunni: Caliph Umar designated six people; this appears in Bukhari (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 3700). In the Sunni reading, he broadened the consultation by choosing people with whom the Prophet was pleased, and the result was completed with Medina's approval.
disputes.1.shia: The six appear in Bukhari (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 3700). In the Shia reading, Imam Ali's being treated on a par with the others and the authority remaining with Abd al-Rahman b. Awf are mentioned in the Shiqshiqiyya as an arrangement that affected the outcome from the start.
disputes.2.title: ihla63
Imam Ali's answer to the condition of conduct
disputes.2.sunni: Al-Tabari reports that Imam Ali said "my own ijtihad." In the Sunni reading, this is his preservation of his scholarly independence.
disputes.2.shia: Al-Tabari reports that Imam Ali said "my own ijtihad." In the Shia reading, he did not bind himself to the practice of the two earlier caliphs but took the Book, the sunna and his own ijtihad as the basis.
questions.0: Caliph Abu Bakr, before appointing Caliph Umar, had Abdurrahman b. He met with Avf and Uthman. Why do you think Ali was not consulted?
questions.1: Caliph Umar counted six people there, and Ali was among them. Why do you think Ali's board membership didn't mean he was elected?
questions.2: And he said, "O my people! He left it with Avf. Why do you think the decision at the end of these periods is that Abdurrahman b. It's in the hands of Avf?
questions.3: Abdurrahman b. Forgiveness is conditional upon the Book, the Sunnah, and the way of the two caliphs before them. Why do you think Ali didn't take the path of the previous two caliphs as a condition and said "one according to my own intuition"?
summary: Caliph Abu Bakr chose Caliph Umar in his place. When Caliph Umar was wounded, he left a six-man shura; Abd al-Rahman b. Awf chose Uthman. In the Shia reading, this shura, Imam Ali's saying "my own ijtihad" and the Shiqshiqiyya describe his place.
key: A caliphate by appointment, a narrowed shura
notes.0: Before dying, Caliph Abu Bakr appointed Caliph Umar as caliph.
notes.1: When Caliph Umar was wounded, he left the matter to a six-man shura.
notes.2: The members of the shura were: Imam Ali, Uthman, Zubayr, Talha, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman b. Awf.
notes.3: Imam Ali did not accept Abd al-Rahman's condition, and Uthman was chosen.
notes.4: Imam Ali's complaint about this process appears in the Shiqshiqiyya sermon in Nahj al-Balagha.
sunni.5.says: Mu'teziliyli scholar Ibn Abi'l-Hadîd and Hanefi scholar Sıbt Ibn-Cevzi, transmit his message to Shikshikyy. The Sunni mainstream disputes the attribution of the sermon to Ali.
